headline: Chattogram trader attempts suicide on Facebook Live over extortion claims
summary: Sumon Ghosh, 48, drank a poisonous substance during a live broadcast, accusing three men of extorting him and forcing him to sign over his shop lease.
details: Sumon Ghosh, a 48-year-old spice shop owner in Boxirhat, Chattogram, attempted to take his own life by drinking what he said was poison during a Facebook Live broadcast on Friday.
In the viral video, Ghosh accused three brothers—Shamsher Ali, Shahadat Ali, and Ayub Ali—of posing as BNP members to extort money from him.
He claimed the trio had him jailed for five months by falsely labeling him an Awami League supporter, during which time they pressured his wife to sign over the shop's lease.
Ghosh stated he has been paying rent to the legitimate owner of the property since 1996 and has no dispute with anyone else.
Before the attempt, he urged social media users to share the video so that Prime Minister and BNP Chairman Tarique Rahman could see it and take action against those using party names for extortion.
He was rushed to Chattogram Medical College Hospital (CMCH), where doctors say he is currently stable and receiving treatment in Ward No. 14.
Kotwali Police are investigating the matter, while a Chattogram city BNP Member Secretary questioned if Ghosh had previously sought legal remedy for the alleged extortion.
caption:
A Chattogram trader drank poison on Facebook Live to expose alleged extortionists.

Sumon Ghosh, a 48-year-old spice shop owner in Boxirhat, Chattogram, attempted to take his own life by drinking what he said was poison during a Facebook Live broadcast on Friday.

In the viral video, Ghosh accused three brothers—Shamsher Ali, Shahadat Ali, and Ayub Ali—of posing as BNP members to extort money from him.

He claimed the trio had him jailed for five months by falsely labeling him an Awami League supporter, during which time they pressured his wife to sign over the shop's lease.

Ghosh stated he has been paying rent to the legitimate owner of the property since 1996 and has no dispute with anyone else.

Before the attempt, he urged social media users to share the video so that Prime Minister and BNP Chairman Tarique Rahman could see it and take action against those using party names for extortion.

He was rushed to Chattogram Medical College Hospital (CMCH), where doctors say he is currently stable and receiving treatment in Ward No. 14.

Kotwali Police are investigating the matter, while a Chattogram city BNP Member Secretary questioned if Ghosh had previously sought legal remedy for the alleged extortion.

headline: 7 more children die from measles symptoms in Bangladesh
summary: Experts express alarm as many children remain unvaccinated despite a slight decrease in overall infections.
details: Seven more children have died after exhibiting symptoms of measles, according to recent reports.
While the overall rate of measles infections has seen a slight decrease, health experts remain deeply concerned.
The primary cause for alarm is the high number of children who remain outside the vaccination coverage.
Experts warn that this gap in immunization leaves a significant portion of the child population vulnerable to outbreaks.
The situation highlights the urgent need to ensure all children receive their scheduled vaccines to prevent further fatalities.
